newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian refiners locking in profits as prices soar.
newsitem.headline: Asian refiners locking in profits as prices soar.

text.p: Refineries in Singapore and Thailand are running at maximum levels as they enjoy their best profit levels since the first quarter of 1996, industry sources said on Wednesday.

The refiners who had cut output as recently as November are now looking to reap the rewards of rising prices of diesel, jet-kerosene, fuel oil and naphtha and falling crude prices as the market enters a period of peak demand.
Primary margins - the first stage of crude refining - in Singapore have risen to around $2.00 per barrel, after falling into the red in the third quarter, refining sources said.
Refiners are, however, wary their good fortune could be shortlived due to the high volatility of crude and product prices.
"The markets have been very volatile in the past few months. A large part of our profits were due to the big fall in crude prices recently," one refining source said.

If the winter season in the northern hemisphere proves warmer than usual margins would weaken. And the ups and downs for profits so far this year have left most refiners cautious about the future anyhow.
Benchmark prompt Brent crude futures on the International Petroleum Exchange have fallen from a post-Gulf War record of $25.06 a barrel in October to $22.74 on Tuesday.
But while crude prices have been falling, products prices in Asia have remained firm and some, like diesel, have hit fresh five-year peaks.
On Tuesday diesel traded at a new five-year high of $31.50 a barrel for Singapore loading, up 70 cents from the previous record hit in mid November.
Jet fuel prices have also skyrocketted due to renewed purchases by North Asian countries for the winter heating market.
On Friday, jet fuel, or kerosene, traded in Singapore at a post winter high of $32.30 a barrel. This week prices were assessed a dollar higher.
The refiners in Singapore and Thailand are raising production to the maximum to make up for the poorer returns they received in the third quarter.

In the third quarter and at the start of the fourth quarter, Singapore's four refiners operated at below their normal 1.2 million barrels-per-day (bpd) capacity because of voluntary production cuts and plant shutdowns for maintenance work.

Shell Singapore brought down a 200,000-bpd unit for maintenance between July 8 and September. Singapore Refining Co shut down a 60,000-bpd crude unit for one week in October for unscheduled maintenance.

Mobil Oil Singapore reduced production by 10,000-bpd between mid-June and end-August. Esso Singapore, an affiliate of Exxon Corp, reduced runs by 15 percent at its 230,000-bpd refinery between early July and end-October.
On their part, Thai refiners, who produce at 760,000 bpd, also lowered crude runs and shut down units for maintenance in the third quarter and at the start of the fourth quarter.
Thai Oil Co Ltd 1409.HK shutdown a 50,000-bpd unit for 18-days on November 1 and Esso Thailand, an affiliate of Exxon Corp, reduced runs by 10-15 percent in October and early November.
Rayong Refinery Co which had cut runs by 20 percent is also now raising production to maximum, sources said.
